editorial:
You meet six college students who think they have one last shot at a dream job at a global IT company. They bond while preparing for the group discussion, and for a while it feels like a feel-good underdog story. Then the company drops the news that only one person will be hired, and the mood shifts fast. The next day, mysterious envelopes show up, each one holding a secret about someone in the group. Suddenly, trust is gone, and every smile looks suspicious. The movie keeps you guessing about who is lying and why, turning a simple job interview into a tense, personal mystery.

What stands out is how quickly the story moves and how natural the young cast feels. The twists are fun, the pacing rarely drags, and the secrets are messy enough to keep you invested. On the downside, some side characters could use more depth, and a few reveals feel a little rushed. Still, if you enjoy whodunit-style tension with a modern workplace twist, this is an easy recommendation. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or add the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection if you want the sharpest picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the students confront each other during the interview, and the quiet member admits he sent the envelopes to force everyone to be honest. Just when it seems he is the liar, the hiring manager reveals the company never planned to hire any of them; the whole process was a test of loyalty and teamwork. The students leave angry but united, and one of them later receives a real job offer after refusing to play along.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves tense mystery movies with young casts and clever twists.
